issues.quote: the dealer forwards inquiries only; appointment and credit-app leads wait for step 1 (Q23).
issues.concern: Step 0 is now only as safe as the dealer's forward rule, and the dealer told us in writing they would send both inquiries and applications. Nobody has confirmed their system can split those apart. If one credit applicant or one online-appointment customer slips through, Ava sends the standard opener and pushes them to book, under my store's name, and nothing on this page tells anyone it happened.

Name who reviews the morning handoff for a mis-forwarded lead and who calls that customer.

issues.quote: Those two types keep all follow-up off until reply and follow-up carry the type; reschedule replies become a BDC task (Q27).
issues.concern: Turning the follow-up cadence off does not stop the second text. When the customer answers 'thanks, see you Tuesday', the reply turn is whatever agent picks it up, and if it does not see the appointment it pushes them to book again. That is the exact failure the VP Marketing asked us to avoid, one message later. Q12 blocks step 2 only in the sense of being answered; nothing says what happens if the answer is no.
issues.because: E6, E5; Q12; `conversational-ai-backend:src/sequence-workflows/services/sequence-task-message-generation.service.ts:389` (shared generic prompt, per r1 resolution)
issues.ask: State that step 2 does not ship for appointment and credit-app types unless the reply turn carries the type and appointment (Q12 answered yes), or put carrying it into step 2 scope.

issues.quote: appointment confirms use date, time and store, or no specifics if one is missing.
issues.concern: A missing value is handled. A wrong one is not. If the parse reads the wrong store or the wrong time, Ava confidently confirms it, the customer drives to the wrong rooftop or arrives at the wrong hour, and my store finds out when they are standing at the desk. No detection, no owner.
issues.ask: Put every Ava-confirmed appointment (date, time, store) in the morning handoff so the named BDC role checks it against the store's own board before open, and name that role as the one who calls the customer on a mismatch. Count mismatches in the first two weeks as a step 2 acceptance check.
